h1: The 4 Best 4-Slice Toaster Ovens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 4 best 4-slice toaster ovens for 2026, from air fry models to compact budget picks, with specs and who each suits.
summary: The BLACK+DECKER air fry model is our top pick for buyers who want one countertop appliance to toast, bake and crisp. The natural convection BLACK+DECKER is the safer choice if you never plan to air fry. Elite Gourmet's ETO490 offers a 9L cavity at a lower bucket, and the ETO449X is the smallest footprint of the group.
intro: The most common mistake with a 4-slice toaster oven is trusting the label. Four slices of bread across fits very differently from a four-slice cavity that only holds them in two rows, and a 9L interior behaves nothing like a 12-inch pizza oven. Before you compare features, decide what you will actually put inside.

We ranked four models on cooking features (air fry, convection, pizza function), stated capacity, power, and the price bucket each sits in. Everything here comes from listing specs, so treat wattage and capacity as the starting point and check the dimensions against your counter.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Air Fry Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The only pick here that adds air frying to a 4-slice body.
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER pairs a 4-slice cavity with an air fry mode, which is rare at the $50-100 bucket. It lets one appliance replace both a toaster and a small air fryer on a crowded counter.

It ranks above the natural convection BLACK+DECKER because air fry circulates hot air harder, so wings and fries crisp rather than just warm through. The tradeoff is that a small cavity limits batch size, so you will cook in rounds.

Buy it if you want a single compact appliance for toast, reheating and crisping. Skip it if you only toast bread, since you are paying for a mode you will not use.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want toasting and crisping in one appliance.
products.skipIf: You only make toast and never fry.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven with Natural Convection
products.verdict: A convection 4-slice oven for buyers who skip the air fry premium.
products.description:
This model keeps the 4-slice footprint and adds natural convection for more even baking than a plain radiant oven. It sits in the same $50-100 bucket as the air fry version.

It lands second because it lacks a true air fry mode. If crisp results matter, the pick above handles that better; if you mostly bake, broil and toast, this one gives up little.

It suits households that want even heat for toast and small bakes without extra settings. Skip it if crispy fried-style food is the reason you are shopping.
cons: Same price as air fry model
products.idealFor: Bakers and toast eaters who want even heat without extras.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO490 9L/4-Slice Oven
products.verdict: A 9L cavity at the $25-50 bucket for light daily use.
products.description:
The ETO490 offers a 9L, 4-slice interior in the $25-50 bucket, roughly half the cost of the BLACK+DECKER models. That makes it the sensible entry for dorms and first apartments.

It ranks below the BLACK+DECKER pair because the listing shows no convection or air fry mode, so cooking is basic radiant heat. You trade features for price.

Buy it for toast, bagels and reheating. If you want even baking or crisping, step up a bucket.
products.idealFor: Dorms and first apartments on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You need convection or air fry.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO449X Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The smallest footprint here, with a pizza function on top.
products.description:
The ETO449X is an 800W, roughly 9L oven with a pizza function, sitting in the $25-50 bucket. It is the most compact of the four.

It ranks last because 800W is modest and the cavity is the tightest, so four slices will be a snug fit and heat-up will lag stronger models. Its edge over the ETO490 is the pizza setting.

It works for a small counter or a single person. Anyone cooking for a family should pick a larger model.
products.idealFor: Single users with very limited counter space.
products.skipIf: You cook for three or more people.

whatMatters.detail: A 4-slice label describes how much bread fits, not the real interior. Liter volume gives a better sense: 9L is tight for anything beyond toast. Check the interior dimensions on the listing, and measure the dish you would use.

Air fry blows hot air quickly across food for a crisp finish, while natural convection gives gentler, more even heat. Air fry matters if you cook frozen fries or wings. Look for the mode named in the title or bullet points.
Wattage governs how fast the oven heats and recovers after you open the door. Low-power models like 800W units run slower on larger loads. Check the watt figure on the spec sheet before you buy.

Toaster ovens throw heat out of the back and sides, so you need clearance, plus space above for a hinged door. Tight counters under cabinets can be a problem. Read the exterior dimensions and leave a few inches free.
Crumbs and grease build up on the bottom, which affects smell and fire risk. A pull-out crumb tray makes upkeep quick. Look for crumb tray mentions in the feature list.

faq.q: Does a 4-slice toaster oven fit a pizza?
faq.a: Usually only small personal pizzas. The ETO449X lists a pizza function, but check the listed interior size against your pizza.

faq.q: Is air fry worth it in a toaster oven?
faq.a: It is if you cook frozen or fried-style foods often. If you only toast bread and bake, natural convection is enough.

faq.q: What is the common buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming 4-slice means a large cavity. Liter volume is a better guide to what actually fits.

faq.q: Can I put it under a cabinet?
faq.a: Leave clearance above and behind it. Heat vents out the back and top, so a tight spot can be a hazard.
Unplug it, let it cool, and empty crumbs from the tray or bottom regularly. Wipe the interior with a damp cloth.

faq.q: Is it better than a regular toaster?
faq.a: It is more versatile, since it bakes and reheats too. A basic toaster is faster and simpler for toast alone.

finalTake: The BLACK+DECKER Air Fry model is the one to buy if you want a single capable appliance. The Natural Convection version suits bakers who skip air fry. The Elite Gourmet pair serves budget and tight-space buyers well, as long as you accept simpler cooking.
